issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Perpetrator Cues: Anything that reminds me of the person who harmed me
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Perpetrator Cues' is poorly matched to toxic chemical exposure, which typically does not involve an identifiable person who harmed the patient. This wording implies interpersonal trauma and is hard to reconcile with the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Medical Care: Seeking medical or psychological help
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Medical Care' is not well supported by the rest of the profile. The selected threat and memory items focus on hypervigilance, sleep disruption, vivid recall, numbness, and rage, but nothing else suggests healthcare-related fear or avoidance. As a strategy item it feels disconnected rather than clinically linked.

issues.item: Threat: Night Vigilance: I find it harder to feel safe at night than during the day
issues.explanation: 'Night Vigilance' is weakly grounded in the reported trauma type and the rest of the profile. Toxic chemical exposure more plausibly yields situational/environmental vigilance (odours, enclosed spaces, industrial settings, breathing sensations) than specifically feeling unsafe at night.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Perpetrator Cues: Anything that reminds me of the person who harmed me
issues.explanation: For a toxic chemical exposure trauma, 'Avoid Perpetrator Cues' refers to reminders of a person who harmed me, which implies an interpersonal perpetrator and is hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma type unless there was a distinct human assault component not otherwise represented.

issues.item: Memory: Emotionless Recall: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'Emotionless Recall' and 'Rage on Recall' pull in opposite directions as dominant immediate recall states. Emotional numbing during recall can coexist with anger at other times, but stated together as parallel core memory characteristics without any other context they are clinically conflicting.

issues.item: Avoid Perpetrator Cues: Anything that reminds me of the person who harmed me
issues.explanation: For toxic chemical exposure, 'the person who harmed me' implies an interpersonal perpetrator. That is hard to reconcile with the validated trauma type unless there was a clearly identified human assailant, which is not otherwise represented anywhere else in the profile. The rest of the items describe non-interpersonal post-traumatic responses (vigilance, sleep disturbance, vivid/numb/rageful recall), so this single perpetrator-focused avoidance item is the clinically incoherent element.
